events.title: Friday Night Supper Club
events.description: This is quite a unique night! We think that it’s a great tradition to make at least one Friday night a month a delectable social affair full of good music, good drinks, and fantastic food. On arrival you can expect to be fortified with a glass of your favourite tipple followed by a lively demonstration where we will run through a couple of elements from the evening’s menu. Enjoy a hands-on session where you will get involved in some cooking (generally the starter and dessert), before being seated in the dining room to savour delicious food and company restaurant-style. The supper clubs are highly suitable for both groups as well as those flying solo. Readers are advised to check with the venue before relying on the details published here.

events.title: Dublin by Dusk
events.description: Dublin by Dusk invites locals and visitors to enjoy the city centre in a new way on the last Thursday of each month. Participating venues and businesses will bring their own flavour to the evening, from late openings, tours and pop-up activities to cultural experiences, food and drink offers, shopping promotions and family-friendly options. It is a city-wide invitation to stay a little longer, discover something new and enjoy Dublin’s evening atmosphere across culture, hospitality, retail and visitor attractions. The programme is supported by the Department of Culture, Communications and Sport, Dublin City Council, Fáilte Ireland and Dublin Town, working together with businesses and cultural partners to further re-energise the city centre.

events.title: Irish Mythology Storytelling Experience
events.description: Step into the darker, more powerful world of Irish mythology through this live storytelling performance. Performed entirely from memory, this intimate one-man theatrical show brings Ireland’s legendary heroes, warriors and ancient tales to vivid life. Audiences experience stories of heroism, passion, violence and fate as they were originally told long before they were softened for modern audiences. Designed for mature audiences, this is a unique cultural experience that offers visitors a deeper, more memorable encounter with Irish mythology and storytelling tradition. Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.

events.description: The National Print Museum will open late on the last Thursday of every month from June to October. events.description: Visit Stillgarden Distillery to learn how to craft some of our ground-breaking cocktails from our award-winning liquid experts. events.title: Crash Course On Ireland
events.description: Crash Course on Ireland is a fun and informal two-hour introduction to Irish history and culture, presented by two qualified local tour guides in a traditional Dublin pub. Over a pint, discover the big stories that shaped Ireland – from the Celts, Vikings and Normans through the Famine, 1916, independence and modern Ireland. Along the way, explore Irish music, sport, writers, language, pub culture and some of the quirks of Irish life that visitors often notice but don't quite understand. Every Thursday in September and October, 6.30pm – 8.30pm at Turks Head, Parliament Street, Dublin. Readers are advised to check with the organiser before relying on the details published here.

events.title: 'Thinning the Veil': Art Exhibition
events.description: Six contemporary Fingal artists come together at Malahide Castle this autumn in an exhibition exploring memory, history, heritage and the changing role of monuments in contemporary Ireland. Curated by Eamonn Maxwell, the exhibition features sculptures, installations, sound works and graphic pieces throughout the castle. From 22 September, the programme continues with free special events including a Curator’s Tour & Artist Q&A with Eamonn Maxwell and Deborah Hewson, artist talks and exhibition tours with Ann Ensor, Laura Skehan, Michelle Hall and Susan Buttner, a live performance by Tadhg Kinsella, and a closing night exhibition tour with Cathal Dowd Smith. Advance booking is required for events.

events.title: Dublin By Dusk at EPIC Museum
events.description: On the last Thursday of each month until November, EPIC will remain open until 9pm, with tickets available for just €10 and a special evening guided tour (for €15) with limited availability. Evening museum visits offer a quieter, more relaxed way to experience Dublin's cultural attractions. Visitors can explore at their own pace after work, avoid daytime crowds, and enjoy a different atmosphere in the city's historic Docklands. A museum as tailored for locals as it is for tourists, if you've never visited EPIC, let this be your sign. Discover Ireland's long emigration history, and the global influence of the diaspora in this fully immersive and interactive museum.

events.description: Thursday 1 October 2026 – Sunday 29 November 2026; Wed-Fri 1-6pm, Sat 10am-6pm, Sun 12-6pm Smashing Times Visual Art Gallery, 30 Sandycove Road, Sandycove, Dublin A96V9P1 Free admission. Featuring work by writer Féilim James and visual artists Jessica Rodrigues, Gillian Lambe, Viktoriia Yevsiukova, Hina Khan, Aman Walayat and Mary Moynihan, the exhibition explore peace and human rights, sparking dialogue and new visions for the future. events.title: The Origins of Halloween Tour

Uncover the tragic story of ‘Goody Annie Glover’ the unfortunate Irish woman who became the last person hanged for witchcraft in Boston in 1688 and how the influx of Irish immigrants, who brought their traditions and folktales, helped shape the story of jack-o’-lanterns in America. events.title: Legends, Ghosts and Ghouls of Dublin | Walking Tour
events.description: Ireland has a unique relationship with its legendary past. Kept alive in the histories of the Filí and the Seanchaidhe, Ireland’s gods were not destroyed but - in the words of Mark Williams - demoted to lesser beings. This is an important element of Ireland’s oral histories, which in turn have coloured its popular histories and left many legends for us to parse over today. On the other side of Irish history we have the ballrooms, the salons, and the private studies of Dublin’s litterati. The seances and unwrapping parties, the mysteries and the macabre, all combining into the secret esoteric orders that strove to unlock the secrets of existence. events.title: Grisly tales from the Anglo-Norman advance: horrors of the twelfth century
events.description: Their conquests and institutions reshaped the island’s political and cultural landscape, creating an Ireland of ‘two nations’. This talk explores the violent reality of their impact and how Irish kings sought to respond. It also considers the limits of conquest and the ethnic tensions that emerged as expansion stalled. Political and military deadlock left both communities in limbo, with each increasingly viewing the other as an existential threat. Their worsening relations and deeply felt grievances offer a compelling study of conflict and coexistence, with wider relevance to our understanding of colonial societies. events.title: Lark After Dark: Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde (1920)
events.description: Halloween night begins at The Lark with one of cinema’s earliest and most memorable monsters. Released in 1920, Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde stars John Barrymore as the respectable doctor whose experiments to separate the good and evil within himself unleash the sinister Mr. Hyde. More than a century later, Barrymore’s remarkable transformation remains one of the great performances of early horror cinema. Start Halloween with a 100-year-old tale of science, temptation and the monster within, experienced as cinema should be: on the big screen, together, in the darkness of a theatre. events.title: Halloween & its Creepy Irish Origins
events.description: Want a chilling experience? Not too chilling — we want you entertained, not terrified. But we do venture into the supernatural and the origins behind Halloween customs we still enjoy today. Halloween began as a Christian overlay on the ancient Irish feast of Samhain. The Celts revered their ancestors — and feared them too. On this night, the veil between worlds thinned and spirits, mostly malevolent, walked the land. People devised tactics to protect themselves, customs that survive today as Halloween traditions. Irish writers drew on this folklore for their own spectral creations — The Picture of Dorian Gray, Melmoth the Wanderer, Carmilla, and Dracula. We'll dip into it all, and try not to get splashed in blood!

events.description: Free, inclusive, family-friendly celebration in the grounds of historic Swords Castle. Honouring loved ones who have passed, this culturally authentic event celebrates life and togetherness through music, food, art and remembrance. Brought to you by Swords Castle in partnership with the South and Central American Community. In the restored Chapel see a decorated ofrenda (altar), in memory of recently departed community members. Talks will explain the context and meaning of the celebration. Indoor storytelling for all. Outdoors enjoy Latin American and South American food, then settle in for a screening of Pixar’s Coco. Performers bring the festival atmosphere to life with music and dance. Please dress appropriately for an outdoor event.

events.title: RTÉ CO Presents: A Little Fright Music
events.description: You might know it as Halloween, but the origins of this carnival of all things supernatural lie deep within our Celtic roots – traditions such as trick or treat, apple bobbing and jack o’lanterns were all part of Samhain, the pagan Harvest-time celebration of All Hallow’s Eve. Join us in a musical celebration of this ancient Irish festival - and indulge our continuing love for all things ghoulish, ghostly and chilling of the spine. We’ll certainly put a spell on you, thanks to the RTE Concert Orchestra under the baton of our very own Fright Manager, Mister Guy “Beetlejuice” Barker, with voodoo vocals from “Killer Joe” Stilgoe and Naomi “Vampira” Banks. events.description: A concert for the Faithful Departed – Duruflé Requiem In May 1940 Germany invaded France.
